election._note: Scheduled for 13 September 2026; Wikipedia, '2026 Swedish general election'. Modified Sainte-Laguë in 29 constituencies with 39 adjustment seats, reduced to national PR -- see docs/electoral-systems.md. The statutory gate is the 4% national threshold, standing in for the 12% constituency-qualification half. The Riksdag has been unicameral since 1970, when the bicameral system was replaced by one chamber -- there is no upper block below for that reason, the mirror of GBR's note on why its Lords row exists.

dissolution._note: The Prime Minister, after consulting the Speaker, may order an EXTRA election at any time; it must be held within three months of the order, and a Riksdag elected at one serves only the remainder of the regular electoral period. The power has never been used under the 1974 instrument -- rare in practice, as the rule's name implies -- so no lockout is authored. Regeringsformen, Ch. 9; Wikipedia, 'Extra election (Sweden)'.

amendment._note: Ch. 8 Art. 14 of the Instrument of Government: a constitutional amendment must pass the Riksdag TWICE with a general election in between, the second time with no more than one third of the members against -- in practice the machinery's two_thirds. Regeringsformen, Ch. 8.
amendment._referendum_note: A proposal pending before the Riksdag is put to referendum if one tenth of the members so move and one third vote in favour, held simultaneously with the election intervening between the two votes -- the same optional-stage shape FRA's Art. 89 gives the President's choice. Regeringsformen, Ch. 8 Art. 14.
amendment._permits_system_change_note: No eternity clause: the two-identical-votes procedure is the only bar, and the 1974 Instrument itself was enacted through a total revision, so the form of the state is revisable -- GBR's shape rather than FRA's Art. 89 §5.

judicial._note: No review of primary legislation: the Council on Legislation (Lagrådet) is consultative, and a court may set an Act aside only where its conflict with a fundamental law is EVIDENT (Regeringsformen, Ch. 11 Art. 14) -- a power no Swedish court has ever used to strike a statute. GBR's none, with a thinner footnote than the Human Rights Act's s.4 gives it.

formation._note: The SPEAKER, not the monarch, conducts the talks and nominates a candidate Prime Minister, who takes office unless a MAJORITY votes AGAINST him or her -- abstentions count for the candidate, negative parliamentarism's quiet half (Ch. 6); the monarch has had no role in formation since the 1974 instrument. A censure motion needs a tenth of members to move and carries only with an absolute majority of all members (175 of 349), and even a carried motion does not remove a Government that instead gains a successor through the Speaker within a week -- the machinery's simple_present reads the vote bar and not that constructive escape, a reduction recorded the way AUT's amendment row is. Regeringsformen, Ch. 6, 12 and 13.

government._pretender_note: Whom data/laws/amendments.json's Restoration Act puts on the throne. Authored per nation because the law is generic and the dynasty is not; a monarchy points this at its own sitting monarch.

fiscal._note: General government, IMF/OECD estimates ~2024-2025, rounded, on the same conventions as SVK.json's block. VAT 25% is the statutory standard rate (Tax Foundation, 'VAT Rates in Europe 2025'); corporate 20.6% is the statutory rate since the 2021 change; income 30 is a blend of the ~32% municipal flat with the national progressive step; capital gains 30% is the flat rate on capital income; the net wealth tax was abolished in 2007. Revenue 41.5% of GDP is the OECD Revenue Statistics figure. Debt ~44% of GDP (Eurostat/Riksgälden, 2024), with the pensions line the lightest in this register -- the premium-pension system pushed the old pay-as-you-go liability down. The spending split is the V1.2a policy split, not a reconciliation of the accounts.
